startup.name: Sarvam AI
startup.appears_to_be: India-focused sovereign AI platform offering model APIs, multilingual voice agents, document digitisation, dubbing/content transformation, and enterprise workflow agents.
startup.audience: Observed: developers, enterprises, government teams, content teams, and regulated organisations. Inferred: teams that need Indian-language AI with India-based deployment and governance.
startup.problem: Observed: generic AI and OCR tools struggle with Indian languages, scripts, complex documents, and production governance. Inferred: organisations need to serve Indian-language users without giving up operational control.
startup.promise: Observed: build and deploy frontier-class, population-scale AI from India, with support for Indian languages, sovereign compute, and enterprise controls.
startup.mechanism: Observed: APIs and SDKs for speech, text, translation, document AI, and dubbing, plus managed products for voice agents, content transformation, document workflows, and enterprise agents.
startup.primary_action: Sign up / Get Started, generally routed to dashboard.sarvam.ai; enterprise visitors can use Contact Us or Talk to Sales.
startup.alternative: Observed: use separate model, speech, OCR, dubbing, or agent platforms; inferred: international AI APIs or specialist Indian-language vendors.
evidence_notes: Observed — Homepage hero: ‘AI for all from India’ and ‘Built on sovereign compute. Powered by frontier-class models.’
Observed — Homepage product surface: Text to Speech, Speech to Text, Voice Agents, Document Digitisation, and Dubbing.
Observed — Docs: production-ready APIs for transcription, translation, transliteration, text-to-speech, and conversational AI.
Observed — Trust Center: ISO 27001:2022 and SOC 2 Type II are presented as certified; ISO 42001 is presented as in progress.
Inferred — The strongest initial wedge is India-language infrastructure and enterprise deployment control, not a single narrowly defined product.

verdict.label: Launch after critical fixes
verdict.summary: Sarvam presents a credible, unusually complete India-focused AI platform with strong product breadth, developer documentation, enterprise proof, and visible trust infrastructure. Launch readiness is held back by contradictory pricing/credit information, a stale event banner, and an ambiguous sign-up destination that weakens the primary next step.
verdict.strongest_asset: The combination of concrete product pages, an accessible API documentation journey, customer evidence, and a detailed Trust Center gives qualified buyers multiple ways to validate the platform.
verdict.biggest_risk: A buyer comparing the pricing page can see materially different bonus-credit and free-credit claims, while the main sign-up link redirects to indus.sarvam.ai rather than an obviously named general dashboard.
verdict.retest_condition: Recheck pricing and credit values across every pricing surface, replace or date-bound the Epoch banner, and make the primary sign-up destination explicitly match the intended onboarding experience on desktop and mobile.

dimensions.name: Positioning clarity
dimensions.finding: The homepage clearly states India focus, sovereign infrastructure, frontier models, and population-scale ambition, while product pages clarify individual offers.
dimensions.evidence: Homepage hero and product navigation; Studio, Akshar, Arya, and Voice Agents pages each have specific outcome-led headlines.
dimensions.recommendation: Make the platform entry point more scannable by naming the two primary journeys—build with APIs versus buy an enterprise application—above the fold.

dimensions.name: Audience relevance
dimensions.finding: Audience cues are visible for developers, enterprises, government, BFSI, content teams, and regulated organisations.
dimensions.evidence: Homepage labels ‘Enterprise | Government | Developers’; product pages list use cases such as BFSI, education, publishing, public records, and customer operations.
dimensions.recommendation: Add a short role-based chooser or segmented CTA so visitors can self-select API, product, or enterprise deployment paths faster.

dimensions.name: Conversion path
dimensions.finding: Sign Up, Get Started, Try the API, Try Studio, and Contact Us CTAs are repeated and generally point to viable public destinations.
dimensions.evidence: Homepage and product pages expose multiple CTAs; contact form is visible; dashboard.sarvam.ai redirects to indus.sarvam.ai, creating destination ambiguity.
dimensions.recommendation: Use a named destination such as ‘Open Sarvam Platform’ or route the CTA to the actual general onboarding page; state what happens after sign-up.

dimensions.name: Product proof
dimensions.finding: Sarvam shows code, API scope, product-specific workflows, case-study outcomes, named customer testimony, demos/scenario language, and operational metrics.
dimensions.evidence: Homepage code sample and 10B+ tokens/<100ms/99.9% claims; Tata Capital quote; Voice Agents, Studio, Akshar, and Arya feature details.
dimensions.recommendation: Attach the strongest quantitative claims to named case studies, benchmarks, methodology, or date labels so visitors can distinguish proof from marketing claims.

dimensions.name: Trust and risk
dimensions.finding: Trust content is unusually detailed, but the pricing page contains contradictory free-credit and bonus-credit statements.
dimensions.evidence: Pricing page says every plan starts with ₹1,000 free credits, then shows Starter ₹300 bonus, Pro ₹1,000/₹2,000 bonus, and Business ₹7,500/₹12,500 bonus in different sections; Trust Center lists certifications and requestable reports.
dimensions.recommendation: Create one source of truth for credits, pricing, expiry, refunds, and billing; add last-updated dates and link the pricing table from docs and dashboard.

dimensions.name: Experience quality
dimensions.finding: Information hierarchy and navigation are strong in the public text surface, but responsive behavior, focus states, interaction feedback, and visual loading could not be verified because the integrated browser was unavailable.
dimensions.evidence: Rich page structure, repeated global navigation, product-specific sections, and accessible-looking form labels are visible in the public crawl; viewport-level inspection was unavailable.
dimensions.recommendation: Run a real desktop/mobile QA pass covering nav menus, cards, language selectors, audio/demo controls, form errors, focus order, and overflow at 320px, 768px, and 1440px.

dimensions.name: Technical surface
dimensions.status: Good public coverage with verification gaps
dimensions.finding: Public product, docs, pricing, status, legal, and contact paths are discoverable; docs include quickstart, SDKs, API reference, errors, rate limits, and status links.
dimensions.evidence: Docs welcome page exposes quickstart and reference links; status page reports fully operational; API and product links resolve in the public crawl. Console errors, metadata/social cards, and real responsive rendering were not observable.
dimensions.recommendation: Add automated link, metadata, console-error, and viewport checks to release QA; verify every dashboard and product subdomain redirect is intentional.

dimensions.name: Launch operations
dimensions.finding: Pricing, support, security contact, status, documentation, and enterprise contact paths are present, but expectation-setting is weakened by stale campaign copy and unclear post-CTA behavior.
dimensions.evidence: Homepage says ‘Sarvam Epoch is happening July 30 and 31’ while the audit date is August 4, 2026; docs expose support paths; Trust Center states a two-business-day security response.
dimensions.recommendation: Remove expired banners, publish onboarding and support expectations beside each CTA, and ensure pricing/support promises match across site, docs, and dashboard.

journey.observation: The hero names Sarvam as an India-focused sovereign AI platform and gives a clear high-level promise.
journey.consequence: A relevant visitor can orient within five seconds, though the platform breadth is broad.
journey.fix: Preserve the hero and add an explicit API-versus-enterprise choice.

journey.observation: Product categories, API examples, and product pages explain what can be built and who each product serves.
journey.consequence: Visitors can form a credible mental model, with some risk of category overload.
journey.fix: Use role-based navigation or a short ‘Choose your path’ module.

journey.observation: The site provides code, docs, named products, case-study outcomes, customer testimony, product scenarios, and operational metrics.
journey.consequence: Qualified buyers have enough public material to continue evaluation.
journey.fix: Add methodology and source links for the largest performance and ROI claims.

journey.observation: Trust Center, status page, pricing, deployment options, and legal links are public, but pricing/credit sections disagree and some security documents require request/NDA.
journey.consequence: Buyers may pause to reconcile cost or request assurance before trying the platform.
journey.fix: Resolve pricing contradictions and label which trust evidence is public versus request-only.

journey.observation: CTAs are prominent, but the general sign-up link resolves from dashboard.sarvam.ai to indus.sarvam.ai, which is not self-explanatory as a general onboarding destination.
journey.consequence: A visitor may wonder whether they reached the intended platform or a separate product.
journey.fix: Align CTA label, URL, and destination naming; add a clear next-step sentence.

journey.observation: Pricing describes plans and support, but the page has conflicting credit values; the homepage also carries an expired event message.
journey.consequence: Visitors cannot rely on the page as the final source of truth for cost or current availability.
journey.fix: Publish a dated, canonical pricing table and remove expired campaign copy.

improvements.title: Resolve pricing and credit contradictions
improvements.evidence: The pricing page says all plans start with ₹1,000 free credits, while later sections show different bonus-credit amounts for Starter, Pro, and Business.
improvements.consequence: Developers and procurement teams may doubt the offer or delay signup.
improvements.change: Keep one canonical table with price, paid credits, bonus credits, total credits, expiry, rate limit, support, and effective date; remove conflicting summary copy.
improvements.validation: Compare homepage, pricing page, docs pricing, and dashboard values against one approved source of truth.

improvements.title: Make the sign-up destination unambiguous
improvements.evidence: The visible CTA is ‘Sign up’ to dashboard.sarvam.ai, but the public destination redirects to indus.sarvam.ai.
improvements.consequence: Visitors may interpret the redirect as a broken or product-specific journey.
improvements.change: Route to the general platform onboarding page or relabel the CTA as ‘Open Sarvam Indus’; add a short description of the next step.
improvements.validation: Open every primary CTA from homepage, product pages, pricing, and docs; confirm destination title and first action match the label.

improvements.title: Remove or date-bound the Epoch banner
improvements.evidence: The footer says ‘Sarvam Epoch is happening July 30 and 31’ during an audit dated August 4, 2026.
improvements.consequence: The company appears inattentive to currentness, especially to new visitors evaluating operational maturity.
improvements.change: Replace with an archive/recap link or hide the banner after the event end date using a scheduled flag.
improvements.validation: Revisit the homepage after the event end date and confirm no present-tense campaign copy remains.

improvements.title: Create a platform-path chooser
improvements.evidence: The site presents APIs, four named products, multiple model families, enterprise deployment, and several audiences in one global journey.
improvements.consequence: A visitor can understand Sarvam but still be unsure where to start.
improvements.change: Add three cards near the hero: ‘Build with APIs’, ‘Deploy an enterprise agent’, and ‘Transform content or documents’, each with audience, time-to-value, and CTA.
improvements.validation: Run a five-second test and ask visitors to identify their next step and intended product.

improvements.title: Substantiate the strongest quantitative claims
improvements.evidence: Pages use claims such as 2x sales conversion, 10x ROI, 114% better, 100M+ conversations, and <24 hours to deploy without visible methodology on the inspected pages.
improvements.consequence: Sophisticated buyers may discount the claims as generic marketing.
improvements.change: Pair each claim with a named customer, sample size or benchmark, timeframe, and linked case study or methodology note.
improvements.validation: Ask five target buyers which proof claims they trust and whether they can find supporting detail within one click.

improvements.title: Run responsive and interaction QA
improvements.evidence: Responsive rendering, mobile nav, focus states, audio controls, form error states, and console behavior could not be verified in the available inspection surface.
improvements.consequence: A visually strong desktop journey could still fail on common mobile or keyboard paths.
improvements.change: Test 320px, 390px, 768px, and 1440px widths plus keyboard-only navigation and error recovery for contact/signup paths.
improvements.validation: Record a pass/fail matrix for each path and capture screenshots of any clipping, overlap, or unreachable control.

rewrites.before: Built on sovereign compute. Powered by frontier-class models. Delivering population-scale impact.
rewrites.after: Build Indian-language AI with production APIs—or deploy sovereign voice, document, and workflow agents for your organisation.
rewrites.reason: Preserves the sovereign positioning while making the two primary buying journeys immediately actionable.
Avoids promising a generic signup when the observed destination resolves to a product-specific domain.

rewrites.before: Sarvam Epoch is happening July 30 and 31
rewrites.after: Sarvam Epoch: watch the July 30–31 recap
rewrites.reason: Keeps the event discoverable without presenting a past event as current.

rewrites.before: Every plan starts with ₹1,000 in free credits.
rewrites.after: New accounts receive [approved amount] in credits. See the dated plan table below for bonus credits, rate limits, and support.
rewrites.reason: Removes a blanket claim until the canonical credit policy is approved and synchronized.

Fix or relabel the sign-up destination
Remove or date-bound the Epoch banner
Add effective dates to pricing and event copy
plan.done_when: All public surfaces tell the same story about cost, current availability, and the first action.

actions: Align CTA labels, URLs, and destination headings
Link docs pricing and quickstart from the relevant CTA
plan.done_when: A developer and an enterprise buyer can each reach the correct next step without interpreting a redirect.

actions: Attach methodology or named case studies to quantitative claims
Clarify public versus request-only trust evidence
Add a dated pricing FAQ covering credits, expiry, refunds, and invoices
plan.done_when: A qualified buyer can verify the top claims and answer basic procurement questions from public pages.

actions: Run broken-link, redirect, metadata, social-preview, and console-error checks
plan.done_when: The primary journey passes on desktop/mobile and all intentional redirects are documented.

actions: Recheck pricing against dashboard and docs
Run one small CTA experiment with a measurable success signal
plan.done_when: No high-severity finding remains open and the next launch experiment has a baseline and owner.

strengths: Strong public breadth across APIs and applications
Useful developer documentation with quickstart, SDKs, reference, rate limits, errors, and status
Named customer testimony and case-study outcomes
Detailed Trust Center with certifications, controls, deployment options, and security contact
unknowns: Authenticated onboarding and actual account activation
Real conversion, activation, retention, satisfaction, and support data
Billing, cancellation, refunds, invoices, credit expiry, and quota behavior after signup
Production monitoring and incident response beyond public status/trust claims
Actual responsive layout, accessibility conformance, browser console behavior, and performance metrics
Security posture and data flows beyond public claims and requestable documents
Legal and regulatory compliance as a qualified audit matter
retest: Five-second comprehension: identify product, audience, outcome, and next step
Open every primary CTA from desktop and mobile and confirm the destination heading matches the CTA
Check homepage and product-page hierarchy at 320px, 390px, 768px, and 1440px
Keyboard-tab through navigation, demos, language controls, CTAs, and contact form; verify visible focus and recoverable errors
Crawl all public product, docs, pricing, trust, legal, status, and signup paths for broken links and unintended redirects
Validate title, description, canonical, Open Graph, Twitter card, favicon, and structured data on the homepage and pricing page
Reconcile pricing and credit values across marketing site, docs, dashboard, and any checkout surface
Confirm security, privacy, retention, residency, incident, and support claims remain consistent across pages
Record the exact copy/component changed and rerun the same audit checklist

experiment.hypothesis: A role-based path chooser will improve qualified visitors' ability to reach the right product and CTA.
experiment.change: Add three hero-adjacent paths: Build with APIs, Deploy enterprise agents, and Transform content/documents, each with a named CTA.
experiment.measure: CTA click-through to the intended destination and percentage of visitors who correctly identify their next step in a five-second comprehension test.
experiment.success_signal: At least 15% relative improvement in intended CTA clicks and at least 80% correct next-step identification, with no drop in contact-form completion.

limitations: The integrated browser was unavailable, so viewport-level screenshots, live interaction states, console errors, and actual keyboard behavior were not directly verified.
No forms were submitted, no account was created, and no authenticated or billing behavior was tested.
Public-web content can change after the audit date; observations are tied to the consulted pages and crawl date.
validation.legal_note: Trust, privacy, security, DPDP, ISO, SOC 2, and other compliance observations are preliminary product-surface observations, not legal, security, or compliance certification.
